evidence: command-question.mjs:261-264 (post-conversion leftover-ticket cleanup, NOT a precondition)
gaps.detail: A real, wired escalation primitive exists end-to-end: the branch stops (issue stays blocked), authority leaves agent hands, and it is surfaced in Queue and autonomy. What is missing is the canonical contract around it, not the channel. Entry is narrow in AUTHOR and SOURCE STATE, not in ticket existence: no [COMMAND-QUESTION] ticket is required at any point before conversion (round-3 correction, reproduced with zero tickets). This primitive alone does not satisfy §20.2.12 and no such claim is made.
gaps.minimalExtension: Extend the existing primitive, do not replace it: give the descriptor a structured payload carrying the 11 §20.2.12 fields (or an artifact id), and bind it to SPEC version + IMP/Subtask + project. Widen WHO may raise a contradiction and FROM WHAT STATE (a packet owner or reviewer, on a source whose descriptor is not already a Command question), and route architecture/research authority separately from the human gate. Do NOT add a 'ticket-free' entry point: that already exists. The earlier instruction not to reuse [COMMAND-QUESTION] is withdrawn; reusing its conversion path unchanged is recommended.
